claims.text: The baseline FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys are equiatomic, homogeneous, single-phase fcc alloys.
The baseline FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys have high saturation magnetization.
The baseline FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys have low coercivity and exhibit soft ferromagnetism.
Replacing Pd or Pt with Ir produces an equiatomic FeCoNiIr alloy.
Arc melting followed by annealing at approximately 1000–1050 °C for 1 hour under an inert atmosphere is a suitable processing route for FeCoNiIr.
Under the proposed processing conditions, Ir can be randomly incorporated into a uniform, single-phase fcc FeCoNiIr matrix without segregation or ordering.
Ir has significantly higher spin–orbit coupling than Pd or Pt.
The incorporation of Ir enhances local magnetocrystalline anisotropy through spin–orbit coupling.
Increased magnetocrystalline anisotropy produces more effective domain-wall pinning.
More effective domain-wall pinning increases the coercive field.
Ir substitution will preserve the high saturation magnetization associated with FeCoNi.
Equiatomic FeCoNiIr will have at least a 10–20% greater coercivity than FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt.
Equiatomic FeCoNiIr will maintain high saturation magnetization.
The predicted coercivity increase applies only while FeCoNiIr remains equiatomic and single-phase fcc.
Phase segregation or ordering may alter the magnetic properties of FeCoNiIr.
Unforeseen phase transformations and other microstructural factors may affect the coercivity attained in FeCoNiIr.

contradictions.description: The boundary restricts the coercivity prediction to single-phase fcc material, but the falsification rule treats phase segregation or ordering as falsifying the hypothesis. Thus, a sample outside the stated applicability domain is simultaneously treated as a decisive negative test.
